seo.title: Automated Calls From Google: What to Know
seo.meta_description: Why Google may call or text your business automatically, how to tell real calls from scams, and what happens to the information, for Anaheim and Orange County.

h1: Automated Calls and Texts From Google to Your Business: What They Are
answer: Google may make automated calls or send texts or WhatsApp messages to the phone number on your Business Profile, either to confirm details like hours or to complete a customer's request such as booking an appointment. Google says it never asks for payment, credit card details or passwords. Treat automated calls from Google as routine; Anaheim and Orange County businesses should answer genuine requests and ignore anyone asking for money.
key_takeaways: Google may call or text to confirm details.
It may also call on behalf of customers.
Google never asks for payment or passwords.
Updates from calls are reviewed, up to 5 business days.
Calls on behalf of customers are recorded.

sections.heading: Why Google contacts businesses
sections.body_html: Google's help page says it might occasionally use automated calls or texts to the phone number on your profile, to confirm your business details are up to date or to help customers with inquiries. Responding helps keep your information accurate.

sections.heading: How to spot scams
sections.body_html: Google states it will never ask for payment, credit card information or account passwords. If a caller asks for money to keep your business on Google, it is not Google. Do not respond to suspicious calls or texts, click links or provide information.

sections.heading: Calls to confirm business info
sections.body_html: Google says you might get an automated call, text or WhatsApp message to confirm details such as operating hours or whether certain services are available. It describes this as a standard process that does not affect your account standing.

sections.heading: What happens to your answers
sections.body_html: Google says information you provide, including photos and posts, is added to your profile on your behalf, subject to its content policies, and you can edit or remove it later. Updates from these calls are reviewed and marked Pending, and the review can take up to 5 business days.

sections.heading: Calls on behalf of customers
sections.body_html: Google says that when customers use Search or Maps to connect with your business, Google may call you on their behalf to complete requests. These calls are monitored and recorded for quality, and the feature is free for businesses and customers.

sections.heading: What customers can ask Google to do
sections.body_html:
• Book appointments, with details like preferred time, service type and party size.
  • Check current restaurant wait times.
  • Confirm the price and availability of in-store products and services.

sections.heading: Why answering helps
sections.body_html: Each answered request is a potential customer. For a busy salon in Anaheim or a restaurant near the Convention Center, a quick answer to an automated booking or wait-time call can turn into a visit.

sections.heading: Train your staff
sections.body_html: Tell whoever answers the phone that Google may call automatically, that these calls are legitimate when they ask for business details or customer requests, and that real Google calls never ask for money or passwords.

sections.heading: Review collected information
sections.body_html: Google's editing help says you can review information collected through these messages under Edit profile, then Collected info, see its source and date and delete items if needed.

sections.heading: Keep your phone number right
sections.body_html: These calls go to the number on your profile. Make sure it reaches someone who can answer during business hours.

sections.heading: Checklist
sections.body_html:
• Staff know Google may call automatically.
  • Staff know Google never asks for money or passwords.
  • Phone number on profile reaches a person.
  • Collected info reviewed.
  • Suspicious calls ignored and not engaged.

sections.heading: Common mistakes with automated calls
sections.body_html:
• Hanging up on every automated call and missing customer booking requests.
  • Trusting any caller who says they are from Google, even when they ask for money.
  • Clicking links in unexpected texts claiming to be about your listing.
  • Giving staff no guidance, so answers to Google's questions are guessed.
  • Never checking what information has been added to the profile from these calls.

sections.heading: A short script for your front desk
sections.body_html: Give whoever answers the phone a few lines to follow. If an automated call asks to confirm hours or services, answer accurately and briefly, and tell the manager afterwards so the profile can be checked. If it is a booking or availability request on behalf of a customer, treat it like any other customer enquiry. If any caller claiming to be Google asks for a payment, card details, passwords or verification codes, end the call, do not click any links sent afterwards and report it to the manager. Post these points near the phone. For busy businesses in Anaheim and across Orange County, this small step protects the profile and makes sure genuine requests become customers.

sections.heading: An example
sections.body_html: Imagine a nail salon in Anaheim that receives an automated call asking whether it offers gel manicures on Sundays. The receptionist, briefed in advance, answers the questions. A few days later the salon receives a separate call claiming to be Google and asking for a payment to keep the listing active. Knowing Google never asks for payment, the receptionist hangs up and does not click any links.

sections.heading: How this fits your local plan
sections.body_html: This task is one piece of a wider local plan. Google says local results are mainly based on relevance, distance and popularity, so the profile, your website and your reputation all have to agree. A practical order for most Orange County businesses is: get the Business Profile verified and accurate, make the name, address and phone identical everywhere, publish one clear page per service, then build a steady habit of genuine reviews and replies. Each step makes the next one work better, and the same signals help AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Google's AI features describe your business correctly when someone in Anaheim asks for a recommendation.

sections.heading: Questions owners ask us
sections.body_html: Owners often ask whether they can stop automated calls entirely. Google describes these calls as a standard way to keep details accurate and to pass on customer requests, so the better approach is to prepare staff to handle them. Another common question is how to tell a real call from a scam. Real calls ask about business details or a customer's request; scams ask for money, card details, passwords or codes. Owners also ask what to do if wrong details were added after a call. Edit the profile and review Collected info to correct or delete them.

sections.heading: What to do this week
sections.body_html:
1. Brief staff on genuine Google calls.
  2. Check your profile's phone number.
  3. Review Collected info.
  4. Share Google's no-payment rule with the team.

sections.heading: When to get help
sections.body_html: Most of this can be done in-house with an hour or two and careful reading of Google's own help pages. It is worth bringing in help when the stakes are high or the problem keeps coming back: a profile that has been suspended more than once, many locations to manage, a site that keeps failing the same checks, or no time to keep up the routine. A good local SEO partner should explain what they will change and why, point to Google's guidelines rather than promise rankings, and leave you with access to every account. Chimera works this way with businesses across Anaheim and Orange County.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Expect occasional automated calls from Google, answer genuine requests, never give payment or password details, and review collected information. Chimera, based in Anaheim, helps Orange County businesses keep profiles accurate and secure.

faqs.a: Yes. Google may use automated calls or texts to confirm details or on behalf of customers.

faqs.q: Will Google ask me for payment?
faqs.a: No. Google says it never asks for payment, credit card details or passwords.

faqs.q: What happens to the information I give?
faqs.a: It's added to your profile, reviewed and marked Pending for up to 5 business days.

faqs.q: Why would Google call on behalf of a customer?
faqs.a: To book appointments, check wait times or confirm prices and availability.
Google says calls on behalf of customers are monitored and recorded.

faqs.q: Can I remove information from these calls?
faqs.a: Yes, through Edit profile, then Collected info.
